column1: Review
The camera on the Pixel 8a is incredible for this price point. Photos are sharp and vibrant.
Battery life is just average. I barely make it through a full day of heavy use.
Love the new 120Hz screen, it makes scrolling so much smoother than my old 6a.
The phone gets noticeably warm when playing games or recording video.
Best value Android phone you can buy right now. The AI features are actually useful.
The bezels are quite thick compared to the regular Pixel 8, looks a bit dated.
Magic Eraser and Best Take are game changers for family photos.
Charging speed is painfully slow. Takes over an hour to top up.
Perfect size for one-handed use. The matte back feels nice and doesn't attract fingerprints.
Tensor G3 chip performs well for daily tasks, no lag at all.
Disappointed that it still charges at 18W. Come on Google, it's 2024.
The screen is bright enough to see outdoors now, huge improvement.
Good phone but the fingerprint sensor is still a bit hit or miss for me.
I prefer the smaller form factor. It fits easily in my pocket.
Great software experience, clean Android without bloatware.
The plastic back scratches easier than glass, definitely need a case.
Face unlock works well, but only in good lighting.
For $499, you can't beat this camera system. Night sight is magic.
Google Assistant is smarter on this phone, call screening is a lifesaver.
Overall a solid mid-range phone, but the battery drain is concerning.
The 7 years of updates promise makes this a great long-term investment.
Haptic feedback is crisp and premium, unlike other budget phones.
Video quality is okay, but not as good as the iPhone.
Setup was a breeze, transferred everything from my Samsung in minutes.
The Aloe Green color looks fantastic in person!
